language.script_notes: Colombian Spanish as national — this is the country's demographic, political and economic core.

road_furniture.guardrail_type: As national; heavily used on winding mountain roads given the terrain.
road_furniture.curb_style: As national; dense formal infrastructure in Bogotá/Medellín.
road_furniture.km_marker_style: As national; dramatic switchback mountain roads common between cities given the three parallel Andean ranges.

architecture.roof_style: Traditional wooden coffee-farm houses (fincas) with wide eaves in the Eje Cafetero; dense modern high-rise construction in Bogotá and Medellín.
architecture.roof_material: Terracotta tile on traditional Andean/colonial buildings; flat concrete on modern urban high-rises.
architecture.wall_construction: Brightly painted wooden coffee-farmhouse architecture (bahareque construction) is the Eje Cafetero's defining regional signature; dense modern glass-and-concrete high-rises define Bogotá's and Medellín's skylines, set dramatically against steep Andean mountain backdrops.
architecture.wall_color_palette: Vividly painted wooden trim on coffee-region farmhouses; muted grey/glass modern urban towers in the big cities.
architecture.distinctive_building_types: Traditional coffee fincas with steep tin roofs in the Eje Cafetero; Medellín's cable-car (Metrocable) system climbing steep hillside barrios; Bogotá's high-altitude, mountain-ringed modern skyline; colonial towns (Villa de Leyva) elsewhere in the highlands.

nature.vegetation: World-renowned high-altitude Arabica coffee plantations blanket the hillsides of the Eje Cafetero; cool cloud forest and páramo (high-altitude moorland) vegetation at the highest elevations near Bogotá.
nature.terrain: Three parallel Andean mountain ranges (cordilleras) run through this region, separated by deep river valleys; Bogotá itself sits on a high plateau at roughly 2,600m elevation.
nature.climate_signature: Cool and temperate given the high elevation — a marked contrast to the hot coasts and lowlands; frequently overcast/misty in the coffee-growing cloud-forest zone.

vehicles.distinctive_vehicles: Willys Jeeps are a beloved cultural icon specifically in the Eje Cafetero coffee region, used to transport coffee and passengers on steep mountain roads.

google_coverage.camera_generation: Best and most current coverage in the country, concentrated around Bogotá and Medellín.
google_coverage.coverage_notes: Very dense in the major cities; good coverage through the coffee region given its tourism importance.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Shared high-Andean terrain, similar cool cloud-forest climate and colonial mountain-town architecture
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Colombia's yellow plates and Carrera/Calle grid signage differ from Ecuador's road furniture; Colombia's coffee-region Willys Jeeps and bahareque farmhouse architecture are distinctly Colombian.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Same country, same plate/bollard base style
confusion_set.tiebreaker: The Andean interior is cool and mountainous with coffee farms and dense modern cities; the coast is hot and tropical, and the Amazon/Llanos is flat lowland savanna or rainforest — all visually distinct.
